The test image shows a tomato plant completely collapsed/fallen over on black plastic mulch. The plant has wilted entirely, stems lying flat, leaves still somewhat green. This suggests a sudden wilt disease affecting the whole plant. Top candidates: Bacterial_Wilt, Southern_Bacterial_Wilt, Southern_Blight, Verticillium_Wilt.

Now viewing one reference from each of my 4 top candidates:

**Analysis:**

- **Test image**: Tomato plant completely collapsed/fallen flat on black plastic mulch. Leaves still somewhat green, indicating rapid/sudden wilting. No staking visible. Classic whole-plant collapse from stem/crown failure.

- **Bacterial_Wilt** (Bugwood_3): Showed cut-stem streaming test — diagnostic, not field collapse. Bugwood_6 showed wilted plants still upright on stakes, leaves browned — different from test.

- **Southern_Bacterial_Wilt** (Bugwood_1): Also showed bacterial streaming diagnostic test — similar to Bacterial_Wilt references.

- **Southern_Blight** (Bugwood_5, #1568116): Showed tomato plants completely collapsed flat on plastic mulch (white instead of black), with surrounding healthy plants — nearly identical collapse pattern to the test image. Southern Blight (Sclerotium rolfsii) kills the stem at the crown, causing sudden whole-plant collapse.

The test image most closely matches Southern_Blight: sudden whole-plant collapse on plastic mulch, green leaves (rapid death), plant lying flat rather than wilting while standing.
